question.text: 'Mahanadi PE Fund II' (Cat II AIF) holds 18% in 'Konark Tech Ltd' pre-IPO. Konark Tech is now filing its DRHP. Under SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018, what is the lock-in applicable to the Cat II AIF's pre-issue shareholding post-IPO allotment?

answer.text: 3 years, as the AIF is deemed part of the promoter group
No lock-in — AIFs are exempt from ICDR lock-in
6 months from date of allotment in the public issue (or 1 year if majority of IPO fresh-issue proceeds are for capital expenditure)
18 months uniformly, similar to promoter contribution

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Regulation 17 of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018: entire pre-issue share capital (other than minimum promoter contribution) is locked-in for 6 months from date of IPO allotment; if majority of fresh-issue proceeds are for capex, lock-in is 1 year. A Cat II/III AIF's holding is NOT deemed part of promoter group merely due to 20%+ equity unless other ICDR criteria are met. The Trap: Option A wrongly treats 18% equity as promoter status. Option B overstates the exemption. Option D is the minimum promoter-contribution lock-in, not the pre-issue lock-in. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests ICDR as an exit-pathway rule. XV (RA) touches this. XXIV is tangential. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Model lock-in expiries into the fund's exit timeline — a 6-month ICDR lock plus a 3-month underwriter greenshoe plus promoter-signaling window typically means 9-12 months of illiquidity post-IPO. For QIP preferential allotment, the lock-in is 6 months (1 year if capex-heavy use of proceeds). Takeover Regulations 29(1) requires 5%+ shareholding disclosure within 2 working days of allotment.
